title: Nouns 5: Quirky Plurals and Always / Never Plural
description: Three small sets of Russian nouns refuse to follow the regular plural rules: truly irregular plurals (друг → друзья, ребёнок → дети, мать → матери), nouns that exist only in the plural (часы, очки, деньги), and nouns that exist only in the singular (молоко, мясо). All three sets are short, closed, and full of everyday words.
descriptionRussian: Три небольшие группы русских существительных не подчиняются обычным правилам множественного числа: настоящие исключения (друг → друзья, ребёнок → дети, мать → матери), слова только в множественном (часы, очки, деньги) и слова только в единственном (молоко, мясо). Все три группы небольшие и состоят из частотных слов.
intro: This lesson gathers the nouns that ignore every pattern so far. Some rebuild their stem before they take an ending. Two swap themselves out for a completely different word. Others have no singular at all, or no plural. None of it can be worked out from a rule, so there is nothing here to derive: these are short lists to be learned. What earns them a whole lesson is frequency. Friends, children, people, money, glasses, milk. You cannot get through a day of Russian without them.
rules: Some Russian nouns have irregular plurals where the stem itself shifts, not just the ending. The biggest groups: -ья plurals (друг → друзья, брат → братья, сын → сыновья, муж → мужья, стул → стулья, дерево → деревья); -ер- insertion in soft-sign feminines (мать → матери, дочь → дочери); -ен- insertion in -мя neuters (имя → имена, время → времена).
Two everyday nouns have completely suppletive plurals (a different word for the plural). Ребёнок → дети (child → children). Человек → люди (person → people).

Some nouns exist ONLY in the plural (pluralia tantum). A1 core: часы (clock), очки (glasses), ножницы (scissors), деньги (money), брюки (trousers), джинсы (jeans), сутки (24-hour period). To say 'one (pair of) X', use одни: одни очки, одни часы.

Some nouns exist ONLY in the singular (singularia tantum): mass nouns (food, drink, materials) and abstract nouns (emotions, qualities). A1 core: молоко, мясо, сахар, хлеб, соль, любовь, счастье, дружба, мебель. They have no plural in normal Russian.
All three sets are small, closed lists. Each member is learned in context as you meet it.
examples: друг → друзья. (Friend → friends; the г turns into з, and the ending is -ья.)
ребёнок → дети. (Child → children; a completely different word, like 'people' in English.)
мать → матери. (Mother → mothers; a syllable -ер- is inserted before the ending.)
имя → имена. (Name → names; the -мя neuters insert -ен- before the plural ending.)
часы (no singular). (Clock / watch; always plural in Russian. One clock = одни часы.)
молоко (no plural). (Milk; mass noun. Russian does not say 'two milks' the way English sometimes does.)

items.hint: The stem changes here. The г turns into з, and a special ending is added.
items.explanation: Друг has an irregular plural: друзья (the г turns into з, and the ending is -ья).

items.hint: This is one of the suppletive pairs: the plural is a completely different word.
items.explanation: The plural of ребёнок is a completely different word: дети (children), just like English child / children.

items.hint: A whole syllable is inserted before the ending.
items.explanation: Мать and дочь have an unusual plural: a syllable -ер- is inserted before the ending. Мать → матери, дочь → дочери.

items.hint: Молоко is a mass noun. Can mass nouns be pluralised in Russian?
items.explanation: Молоко is a mass noun, like 'milk' in English: it has no plural in standard Russian. The same is true for мясо (meat), сахар (sugar), and соль (salt).

items.hint: Имя is in the -мя neuter set (with время). What syllable do these insert?
items.explanation: Имя is part of the special -мя neuter set. The plural is formed by inserting -ен- before the ending: имена. The same happens with время → времена.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Друг has an irregular plural: друзья (with stem change г → з and the -ья ending).

errorCorrection.sentence: Мои браты пришли в гости в субботу вечером.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: My brothers came to visit on Saturday evening.
errorCorrection.explanation: Брат is irregular: the plural is братья (with the -ья ending). Браты does not exist in Russian.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я очень люблю молоки в кофе по утрам.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I really love milk in my coffee in the morning.
errorCorrection.explanation: Молоко is a mass noun: it has no plural in standard Russian. To say 'I love milk', use the singular: молоко. The same rule applies to other mass nouns: вода, чай, сахар. All stay singular regardless of how much you mean. English allows 'two milks, please'; Russian doesn't.

errorCorrection.sentence: Эти человеки работают в нашей школе.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: These people work at our school.
errorCorrection.explanation: The plural of человек is a completely different word: люди ('people'). Человеки does not exist in Russian; the relationship between человек and люди is like English person / people.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each noun by its plural behaviour.

reviewVocab.definition: a small set of nouns adds -ья in the plural, often with a stem change: друг → друзья (г → з), брат → братья, сын → сыновья, стул → стулья, дерево → деревья.
reviewVocab.example: Друг → друзья. Брат → братья. Стул → стулья.

reviewVocab.definition: nouns that exist only in the plural. To say 'one (of) X', use одни. A1: часы, очки, ножницы, деньги, брюки, джинсы, сутки.
reviewVocab.example: Одни часы. Одни очки. У меня есть джинсы.

reviewVocab.definition: nouns that exist only in the singular. Mass nouns and abstracts. A1: молоко, мясо, сахар, хлеб, соль, любовь, счастье, дружба, мебель.
reviewVocab.example: Я люблю молоко. В комнате новая мебель.
